claims.Finding: After matching attack DWORD+200 and decoded +20, a mismatch in attack DWORD+24 or the entry tag causes the manager to call deferred marking on the old attack, construct a new ATTACK_OBJ with the same external slot address, and write the new pointer into that slot at 3D26ED. The manager does not locally retarget old+720 or require marking success before replacement. Under no intervening helper/writer changes, old and new retain the same external slot address.
claims.Limitations: Valid matching slot, successful allocation and constructor return are required. Opaque helper effects, reentrancy and other writers are not ruled out. The fixture explicitly supplies its memory and helper boundaries; no live caller sequence or reachable normal-game failure is proved.

claims.Finding: The original ATTACK_OBJ deleting wrapper loads QWORD(old+720) at 40F4D9 and stores zero through it at 40F4E0 before common cleanup, without comparing the slot content with old. If the retained address names a valid slot already replaced with new, that local store clears the new registration. Two staged original-instruction fixtures reproduce precisely that store after manager replacement.
claims.Limitations: The later destructor call and unchanged valid old+720 are explicit sequence assumptions. Common cleanup is opaque in the fixture and could have further effects. This proves neither live reachability nor a use-after-free, leak or overall lifetime failure.

claims.Finding: ATTACK_OBJ virtual+24 is 40F610. Its complete body can mark this through 3D0EB0 after selected helper results or an eligible update yielding zero counted entries.
